Experimental Methods, Assumptions, and Procedures 2.1. Preparation of Hierarchical Nanoporous Capsules 2.1.1. Synthesis of High Pore Volume Silica Triblock copolymer poly(ethylene oxide)-b-poly(propylene oxide)-b-poly(ethylene oxide) surfactant P123 (EO20PO70EO20, Mv ~ 5800), sodium metasilicate, acetic acid, ammonium fluoride, and 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (TMB), were purchased from Aldrich and used as received. Methanol (≥99.8%, Macron Fine Chemicals) were used as received. Deionized water was used in all experiments. N used for calcination was Ultra High Purity (UHP) Grade N (Airgas, NI 2 2 UHP300, 99.999% N ). 2 High porous volume mesoporous silica was prepared following the synthesis recipe reported in the literature.20 In the reported synthesis, an emulsion was prepared by adding TMB (60 g) to a homogeneous surfactant solution containing P123 (45.0 g), acetic acid (67.0 g), water (750 g), and ammonium fluoride (0.9 g) at 45°C. To this emulsion, a solution of sodium metasilicate (46.5 g) in water (600 g) preheated to 45°C was poured under vigorous stirring. The resulting white slurry was then kept statically at 45°C for 24 h and aged at 100°C for another 24 h. The product was collected by filtration, washed with DI water, and calcined at 560°C for 6 h. When replicating the exact synthesis procedure for the high pore volume mesoporous silica, the batch was too large to easily process with available equipment and led to samples with no accessible pores, so batches were prepared at 1/20 and 1/10 of the reported size. The calcination conditions and template removal are important for pore formation, but the article neglected to report all of the conditions that are important for calcination, notably the ramp rate. Samples were subsequently prepared using ramp rates of 0.25-1oC/min, different calcination gases, and an additional template extraction step prior to calcination. In addition, template extraction via methanol was explored as an option to controllably remove the template with an additional calcination step to ensure full template removal. 2.1.2. Amine loading in Mesoporous Silica Mesoporous silica SBA-15 (ACS Materials, LLC), diethylenetriamine (DETA, 99%, Sigma- Aldrich), tris(3-aminopropyl) amine (TAPA, 95%, TCI Chemicals), trimesoyl chloride (TMC, 98%, Sigma-Aldrich), anhydrous toluene (99.8%, Fisher Scientific), and methanol (≥99.8%, Macron Fine Chemicals) were used as received. Synthesized high pore volume mesoporous silica was also used as a substrate for amine loading. Amine-loaded sorbents were prepared by wet impregnation. Amines were dissolved in methanol and mixed with SBA-15 or high pore volume mesoporous silica, stirred for 4 h at room temperature (~25°C), then dried under vacuum at room temperature for 24 h to achieve desired weight percentage of amine loading in mesoporous silica. 2.1.3.
